newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes ease with cash, diffs steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes ease with cash, diffs steady.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices drifted lower with cash markets, but discounts for bellwether Alaska North Slope (ANS) remained flat on weak demand from refiners.
Sharp gains on overnight ACCESS put November crude at a new post-Gulf War high of $25.72, and left buyers concerned about profit margins on Tuesday.
"(Refiners) were a little reluctant to jump in at those levels," a West Coast broker said.
November NYMEX crude eased from yesterday's highs early, falling 14 cents by 1150 PDT/1850 GMT.
Cash West Texas Intermediate (WTI) followed NYMEX lower, shedding five to 10 cents to hit $25.35/25.45 a barrel.
Outright prices for ANS eased to $22.95/23.25, with deltas steady at $2.30 less November WTI.
ANS Buyers bid around $2.50 under November WTI, while a major producer continued to offer at $2.10.
Line 63 diffs remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under spot WTI for November delivery.
California heavy crudes rose 15 cent with an increase in Texaco's posted prices on October 14. Kern River crude reached $17.30/17.50 a barrel.
Values for Wilmington crude increased to $18.65/18.75 a barrel.
